knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a Product Containing an Exponential or Logarithmic Function

question.:question/worked-solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)={x}^{2}$ and $v(x)=\ln(x).$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =({x}^{2})^{′}\ln(x)+{x}^{2}(\ln(x))^{′} \\  & =(2x)(\ln(x))+{x}^{2}(\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =2x\ln(x)+x\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =(6 \cos{\left(x \right)})^{′}(\frac{\ln{\left(x \right)}}{\ln{\left(10 \right)}})+(6 \cos{\left(x \right)})(\frac{\ln{\left(x \right)}}{\ln{\left(10 \right)}})^{′} \\  & =(- 6 \sin{\left(x \right)})(\frac{\ln{\left(x \right)}}{\ln{\left(10 \right)}})+(6 \cos{\left(x \right)})(\frac{1}{x \ln{\left(10 \right)}}) \\  & =- \frac{6 \ln{\left(x \right)} \sin{\left(x \right)}}{\ln{\left(10 \right)}} + \frac{6 \cos{\left(x \right)}}{x \ln{\left(10 \right)}}\end{aligned}
$$
